rows.assessment: Katoh and Naitoh 1994, PMID:9317557, scientific Abstract item 3, first clause. Direct namespace-qualified Europe PMC MED match; native VERIFIED. The same sentence contrasts graded cell-body shrinkage with all-or-nothing stalk coiling. This supports the curator-synthesized body/projection-shortening parent, not a universal calcium threshold. Other abstract items use Triton-extracted preparations, not the living-cell injection assay. Calcium-induced calcium release is an assumption, not direct molecular proof. Publisher requests returned 403; full Methods, figures and strain provenance were not accessed.

rows.assessment: Khan et al. 2003, PMID:14624035, scientific Abstract opening sentence. Direct namespace-qualified Europe PMC MED match; native VERIFIED. This supports stimulated shortening of a cytoplasmic projection rather than whole-cell locomotion. Reported calcium dependence and speed apply to this assay, not every member of the parent class. Non-detection of other filaments after fixation is not proof of their absence. Full Methods and figures were not accessed; the publisher's HTTP 200 response was an access challenge, not readable article content. Current taxonomic and culture identities remain unresolved.

rows.assessment: Febvre-Chevalier and Febvre 1992, PMID:1639845, PMCID:PMC2289557, Results, Kinetics of the Contraction, printed page 588, right column. Direct extracted-PDF match with the typeset passage visually checked; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. The primary PDF was retrieved from its Semantic Scholar mirror after official PDF attempts failed. Selected Methods/Results and actual Figures 1 and 3-6 were inspected. Length was measured from head top to stalk base, not isolated cell-body length; graph axes use stalk length. The percentage is study-specific. Natural-seawater responses differ from artificially slowed responses. The specimens were collected near Villefranche and cultured at 14-18 C; current taxonomic identity is not verified. The n=20 initial-length sample is not asserted as independent contraction replication. Microtubule disassembly accompanies shortening, but this study expressly does not establish force production. Its disassembly half-time is not automatically contraction duration. The accessible JATS contains an abstract and PDF pointer, not the complete experimental text.

allocation.scientific_scope: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell actively contracts its body or a cytoplasmic projection, reducing its length or extension.

dispositions: v558 and v604 are the existing narrower axopodial and cell-body classes, not the proposed broader parent.
v5 twitching and v52 type-IV-pilus proposals describe extracellular filaments and locomotion, not cytoplasmic-projection shortening.
Other matched proposal lines concern ROBOT table cells, workflow contracts, kinetocyst discharge or habituation response probability.
CommunityMech matches concern interspecies distance and lanthanide ionic contraction, not active microbial shortening.
The upstream quarantine artifact contains Haloplasma contractile names and taxonomic addresses; an epithet alone is not phenotype evidence or an exact trait record.
FOODON context defines muscle tissue, not an equivalent microbial phenotype. Embedding-code matches concern software contracts and projections.

Pinned/current METPO and the editor contain no contraction/shortening literal match in the structured scan. Active motility and historical retired motility labels are related locomotion leads, not exact identity.

Current and retained trait owners: cell length/division and static shape are not active shortening; type-IV/competence pili are extracellular filaments; durotaxis measures directed migration; gravikinesis mentions vacuoles; kinetocyst discharge and habituation have different endpoints. Only the body and axopodial records are narrower children of this candidate.

Source-cache hits concern injection systems, sponge/metazoan contraction, passive osmotic water loss, taxon mentions or changes in generation time. Existing research does not curate an exact parent, synonym or graph node for this phenotype.

Remote HTML repeats cell-size, locomotion, pilus-retraction and withdrawn-mapping contexts, not an independently proposed contraction parent. All non-HTML match groups were assessed by source role; full compressed JSON was parsed rather than judged from a truncated line.

The additional bare-word owners concern floating-point fused-multiply-add contraction, lanthanide ionic-radius contraction, tocolytic chemical synonyms and narrowing a NaCl growth interval. None denotes the proposed microbial phenotype.

Historical review bundles and generated reports cite prior search receipts, existing children and software contracts. They do not introduce an additional exact class. No exact synonym migration or causal-node grounding was accepted.
Fresh CommunityMech PR2006 changed-file blobs produced no matches for the combined novelty/reservation pattern.

Axopodial contraction of the centrohelid heliozoon Raphidiophrys contractilis was induced by mechanical or electrical stimulation.

native_record_verification.interpretation: Actual record CLI results. Direct full-text matching does not upgrade the native abstract verdict.

scope_decisions: Require a body or cytoplasmic-projection shortening endpoint; generic force production or isometric contractility alone does not establish it.
Do not equate extracellular pilus retraction, isolated molecular-machine contraction, contractile-vacuole cycling or cytokinetic constriction alone with this endpoint.
Passive osmotic shrinkage, death-associated shortening and static short-cell morphology are insufficient.
No universal rate, fractional shortening, calcium threshold, ATP dependence, ecological role or protein mechanism is imposed.
The earlier working label active cellular shortening is not an accepted exact synonym.
No canonical taxa, protein accessions, causal graphs, exact external mappings or organism-level disjointness have been accepted.
